exercises.name: Incline DB Press
exercises.cue: Bench at 30 degrees, shoulder blades pinned down and back before the dumbbells move. Drive the elbows toward each other so the upper chest, not the front delt, takes the load.

exercises.name: Flat DB Press
exercises.cue: Feet planted, ribs down, wrists stacked over elbows at the bottom. Stop one inch short of lockout to keep tension on the chest.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
exercises.cue: Bar over the base of the neck, tuck elbows to about 45 degrees on the way down. Push yourself away from the bar and feel the mid-chest, not the shoulders.

exercises.name: Incline Barbell Press
exercises.cue: Bench at 30 degrees, bar path to the collarbone not the throat. Keep the shoulder blades retracted the whole set so the upper chest owns the rep.

exercises.name: Incline Machine Press
exercises.cue: Set the seat so the handles line up with the top of your chest. Squeeze the handles together as you press and hold the top half-second.

exercises.name: Chest Press Machine
exercises.cue: Seat height so handles sit at nipple line, back flat against the pad. Press and feel the sternum close, not the elbows lock.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Incline Press
exercises.cue: Slide the bench so the bar tracks over the upper chest, not the face. Fixed path means you can chase the stretch at the bottom without balancing.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Press
exercises.cue: Bench positioned so the bar meets the mid-chest, feet wide. Lower slow, touch, and drive without bouncing off the ribs.

exercises.name: Weighted Push-up
exercises.cue: Plate on the upper back, body one straight line from ear to heel. Push the floor away and spread the shoulder blades hard at the top.

exercises.name: Dip
exercises.cue: Lean the torso forward about 30 degrees and keep the elbows tracking back. Go to a comfortable stretch only; chest should burn, shoulders should be quiet.

exercises.name: Assisted Dip Machine
exercises.cue: Set assistance so the last two reps are hard, torso leaned forward. Control the bottom third instead of dropping into it.

exercises.name: Cable Fly
exercises.cue: Pulleys at shoulder height, one foot staggered forward, slight elbow bend locked in. Think of hugging a barrel and squeeze where the hands meet.

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
exercises.cue: Pulleys at the bottom, hands finish at chin height. Lead with the pinkies and feel the upper chest fibers shorten.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
exercises.cue: Seat so the handles are at chest height, back flat on the pad. Hold the squeeze for a full second before letting the arms travel back.

exercises.name: Incline DB Fly
exercises.cue: Bench at 30 degrees, soft elbows that never change angle. Own the stretch at the bottom, then squeeze without clanking the dumbbells.

exercises.name: Seated DB OHP
exercises.cue: Back flat on an upright bench, ribs pulled down so you press not arch. Push the dumbbells slightly in front of the ears and feel the side delt take over.

exercises.name: Standing Barbell OHP
exercises.cue: Squeeze glutes and brace hard so the spine does not become the lever. Move the head back, then through, as the bar passes the forehead.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
exercises.cue: Seat so the handles start at ear height, back glued to the pad. Press up and slightly in; stop just short of locking out.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Seated Press
exercises.cue: Bench upright under the bar so the path clears the nose. Fixed rail means you can push closer to failure safely.

exercises.name: Arnold Press
exercises.cue: Start palms facing you at chin height, rotate as you press. Slow the rotation down; the front and side delt should both light up.

exercises.name: Landmine Press
exercises.cue: Half-kneeling, hips square, bar in one hand at the shoulder. Press up and forward on the arc and keep the ribs stacked over the pelvis.

exercises.name: DB Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Tiny forward lean, elbows slightly bent and leading the hands. Raise to shoulder height only and feel the outer delt, never the traps.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Cable behind the body at the lowest setting, opposite hand on the frame. Constant tension means you can go light and still burn out the side delt.

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Pads on the outside of the upper arms, not the forearms. Drive with the elbows and pause a beat at the top.

exercises.name: Leaning Cable Lateral Raise
exercises.cue: Hang off the upright with the working arm away from the stack. The lean lengthens the delt at the bottom; keep the traps down the whole way.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.cue: Chest on the pad, handles at shoulder height, thumbs down. Open the arms wide and stop when the elbows pass the torso.

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull
exercises.cue: Rope set at eye level, split stance, pull to the forehead. Externally rotate at the end so the knuckles finish pointing behind you.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Reverse Fly
exercises.cue: Chest on an incline bench so the low back never works. Lead with the pinkies and think about pulling the shoulder blades apart, not together.

exercises.name: Rope Rear-Delt Row
exercises.cue: Pulley at chest height, elbows flared to 90 degrees. Row to the collarbones and hold the back of the shoulder tight for a second.

exercises.name: Cable Rope Pushdown
exercises.cue: Elbows pinned to the ribs, small forward lean. Spread the rope at the bottom and lock the elbow without shrugging.

exercises.name: Straight-Bar Pushdown
exercises.cue: Shoulder-width grip, elbows glued to the sides. Push the bar to the thighs and pause at full extension.

exercises.name: Overhead Cable Extension
exercises.cue: Face away from the stack, rope behind the head, ribs down. The long head only grows from that deep stretch, so lower slow.

exercises.name: Skullcrusher
exercises.cue: EZ bar, elbows angled slightly back over the forehead. Lower to just behind the hairline and extend without letting the elbows drift.

exercises.name: DB Overhead Extension
exercises.cue: Seated with back support, one dumbbell in both hands, elbows narrow. Get the full stretch behind the head, then squeeze the triceps hard at lockout.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
exercises.cue: Hands just inside shoulder width, elbows tucked tight to the body. Bar to the lower sternum and drive with the back of the arms.

exercises.name: Weighted Pull-up
exercises.cue: Hang fully, then set the shoulders down before the first inch of pull. Drive the elbows to the back pockets and clear the chin without kipping.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Pull-up
exercises.cue: Parallel handles, slight backward lean, chest up to the bar. Easier on the shoulder than pronated; feel the lat, not the biceps.

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-up Machine
exercises.cue: Set assistance so the last two reps are a grind. Pause one second at the top of every rep instead of racing.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Thighs locked under the pad, small lean back that you hold constant. Pull the bar to the collarbone with the elbows, not the hands.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: V-handle, torso almost upright, ribs down. Think elbows into the back pockets and hold the bottom for a beat.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
exercises.cue: Kneel or sit facing the stack, free hand on the hip. Let the shoulder travel up at the top for extra stretch, then pull it all the way down.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
exercises.cue: Hinge slightly at the hips with locked, soft-elbow arms. Sweep the bar to the thighs and feel the lats without any biceps help.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Row
exercises.cue: Chest sealed against the pad so the low back is fully out of the equation. Row the elbows past the ribs and pause where the shoulder blades meet.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
exercises.cue: Sit tall, knees soft, no rocking the torso. Pull to the navel and let the shoulder blades come apart on the way out.

exercises.name: Machine Row
exercises.cue: Chest on the pad, handles at nipple height. Drive the elbows back and down, and squeeze for a full second.

exercises.name: Single-Arm DB Row
exercises.cue: One hand and one knee on the bench so the spine stays neutral and supported. Row to the hip pocket, not the armpit, and feel the lat stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row
exercises.cue: Chest on the pad, feet planted wide, neutral grip. Pull until the plates nearly touch the pad and control the negative.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
exercises.cue: Bar at hip height, body rigid from heel to ear, heels dug in. Touch the sternum to the bar and keep the hips from sagging.

exercises.name: Barbell Row from Floor
exercises.cue: Unsupported hinge under load — off the table for this client. Use a chest-supported variant instead.

exercises.name: Meadows Row
exercises.cue: Staggered unsupported hinge with a rotational demand — off the table for this client. Use a supported single-arm row instead.

exercises.name: Incline DB Curl
exercises.cue: Bench at 60 degrees, arms hanging straight behind the torso. That stretch is the whole point; curl without letting the elbow drift forward.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Curl
exercises.cue: Elbows fixed at the sides, ribs down, no swing from the hips. Curl to where the forearm is vertical and squeeze there.

exercises.name: Cable Curl
exercises.cue: Stand one step back from the low pulley so tension never drops. Keep the wrists neutral and drive with the biceps, not the shoulders.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
exercises.cue: Neutral grip, elbows pinned, no torso English. Feel the brachialis on the outside of the arm doing the work.

exercises.name: Cable Rope Hammer Curl
exercises.cue: Rope at the low pulley, thumbs up, elbows locked to the ribs. Pull the ends of the rope apart slightly at the top.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl Machine
exercises.cue: Armpits over the top of the pad, seat high enough that the shoulders stay down. Control the bottom third instead of bouncing out of the stretch.

exercises.name: Bayesian Cable Curl
exercises.cue: Face away from a low pulley, arm behind the body, split stance. Maximum stretch under tension; curl without the elbow travelling forward.

exercises.name: Farmer Carry
exercises.cue: Heaviest dumbbells you can hold with the ribs stacked over the pelvis. Walk tall and quiet; the grip and the brace are the whole exercise.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
exercises.cue: One dumbbell only, shoulders and hips level the whole walk. Resist the lean — that anti-side-bend demand is what you are training.

exercises.name: Plate Pinch Carry
exercises.cue: Pinch two smooth plates together at your sides, arms straight. Hold until the fingers give out, not the shoulders.

exercises.name: Wrist Curl
exercises.cue: Forearms on the thighs, wrists hanging past the knees. Let the bar roll to the fingertips, then curl it back up.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl
exercises.cue: Palms down, forearms locked on the thighs. Small range, slow tempo, feel the top of the forearm.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
exercises.cue: Feet mid-platform shoulder width, back and hips flat on the pad. Descend until the hamstring covers the calf and drive through the mid-foot.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.cue: Feet mid-platform, low back never rounding off the seat. Stop the descent the instant the pelvis wants to tuck.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
exercises.cue: Brace hard before you unrack, bar tight on the rear delts. Sit between the hips and keep the torso angle constant out of the hole.

exercises.name: Front Squat
exercises.cue: Elbows high, bar in the front-rack shelf, upright torso. Stop at the depth where the elbows stop dropping.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.cue: Dumbbell at the sternum, elbows inside the knees at the bottom. Sit straight down and let the counterweight keep the chest tall.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
exercises.cue: Feet slightly forward of the bar so the knees track without the low back leaning. Fixed path lets you push a hard set safely.

exercises.name: Belt Squat
exercises.cue: Load hangs from the hips so the spine carries nothing. Best heavy-quad option on a tight-back week.

exercises.name: Walking DB Lunge
exercises.cue: Torso vertical, step long enough that the front shin stays near vertical. Push through the front heel and do not let the back knee crash.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.cue: Step back, not forward, so the front knee stays quiet. Drive through the front heel to stand and keep the hips square.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.cue: Back foot on the bench, front foot far enough forward to keep the shin near vertical. Lean the torso slightly and feel the front glute stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Step-up
exercises.cue: Box height that puts the thigh at parallel, whole foot on the surface. Do not push off the trailing leg — the top leg does all of it.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: Bench under the shoulder blades, chin tucked, ribs down. Finish with a hard glute squeeze at the top and stop before the low back arches.

exercises.name: Machine Hip Thrust
exercises.cue: Pad low across the hips, feet flat and shoulder width. Push through the heels and hold the lockout for a second every rep.

exercises.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
exercises.cue: Pads just below the hip bones, spine neutral, chin tucked. Rise using the glutes and stop level — never hyperextend.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
exercises.cue: Rope between the legs, light load only, soft knees. Push the hips back to a stretch, then snap them forward with the glutes.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.cue: Shoulders on the floor, heels close to the hips. Posteriorly tilt the pelvis first, then lift — no low-back arch at the top.

exercises.name: Conventional Deadlift
exercises.cue: Heavy loaded spinal hinge — permanently off the table for this client. Hip thrust is the strength substitute.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.cue: Heavy loaded spinal hinge — permanently off the table for this client. Use a hip thrust or belt squat instead.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.cue: Loaded spinal hinge under stretch — permanently off the table for this client. Train hamstrings with leg curls.

exercises.name: Good Morning
exercises.cue: Long-lever loaded spinal hinge — permanently off the table for this client. Back extensions cover the pattern safely.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.cue: Hips pressed into the pad, knee joint lined up with the machine axis. Curl all the way and lower over three seconds.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.cue: Lap pad snug, torso upright so the hamstring starts lengthened. Pause hard at the bottom of the curl.

exercises.name: Nordic Curl
exercises.cue: Ankles anchored, hips locked in line with the shoulders. Lower as slowly as you can control and push back up with the hands if needed.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
exercises.cue: Back against the pad, knee axis matched to the machine pivot. Squeeze at full extension for a count, no swinging the weight up.

exercises.name: Sissy Squat
exercises.cue: Hold a support, drive the knees forward and the hips back in a straight line from knee to shoulder. Deep quad stretch is the target, not depth for its own sake.

exercises.name: Cable Kickback
exercises.cue: Ankle strap, torso braced against the frame, standing leg soft. Drive the heel back and stop before the low back extends.

exercises.name: Abduction Machine
exercises.cue: Sit upright, slight forward lean to bias the upper glute. Open slowly and hold two seconds at the end range.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise
exercises.cue: Balls of the feet on the platform, knees straight but not locked. Full stretch at the bottom, two-second squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.cue: Knees under the pad at 90 degrees, toes forward. Slow negatives; the soleus responds to time under tension.

exercises.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
exercises.cue: Feet low on the platform, safeties set, knees soft. Push through the big toe and pause in the stretch.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
exercises.cue: Start from the knees with the pelvis tucked under. Roll only as far as you can hold that tuck — the second the low back arches, you are done.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
exercises.cue: Kneel facing away, rope at the ears, hips fixed in place. Curl the sternum toward the pelvis; do not turn it into a hip hinge.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.cue: Elbows under shoulders, glutes and quads switched on, pelvis tucked. Quality over minutes — end the set when the hips drop.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.cue: Low back pressed flat into the floor before anything moves. Extend the opposite arm and leg slowly and keep breathing.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.cue: Low back sealed to the floor, arms and legs extended just above it. Raise the limbs higher the moment the back lifts.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.cue: Stand side-on to the pulley, hands at the sternum, feet planted. Press straight out and refuse to let the cable rotate you.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.cue: Elbow under the shoulder, body one line, top hip pushed to the ceiling. McGill staple — hold clean sets rather than one long sloppy one.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.cue: Hands under shoulders, knees under hips, spine neutral. Reach opposite arm and leg long without letting the hips tip.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
exercises.cue: Dead hang, shoulders packed down, no swinging. Curl the pelvis up at the top — legs alone is just hip flexors.

exercises.name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
exercises.cue: Back flat against the pad, shoulders down away from the ears. Drive the knees to the chest and tuck the pelvis at the top.

exercises.name: Decline Crunch
exercises.cue: Feet hooked, hands at the temples not behind the head. Peel the spine up one segment at a time and stop halfway.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.cue: Lie flat, hands by the hips, knees at 90 degrees. Lift the hips off the floor using the abs, not momentum from the legs.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
exercises.cue: Loaded spinal rotation — off the table for this client. Pallof press trains the same job by resisting rotation.

exercises.name: Loaded Side Bend
exercises.cue: Loaded lateral spinal flexion straight into the QL — off the table for this client. Suitcase carries cover it safely.

exercises.name: Hanging Windshield Wiper
exercises.cue: Loaded spinal rotation under a long lever — off the table for this client. Straight hanging leg raises instead.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
exercises.cue: Loaded rotation through the lumbar spine — off the table for this client. Anti-rotation work only.

exercises.name: Zone 2 Jog
exercises.cue: Conversational pace, nose breathing if you can hold it. If you cannot speak a full sentence, slow down.

exercises.name: Incline Treadmill Walk
exercises.cue: 10-12 percent grade, 3.0-3.4 mph, hands off the rails. Steps and heart rate without the joint cost of running.

exercises.name: Sprint Intervals
exercises.cue: Full warm-up first, then 15-20 second efforts with 90 seconds easy between. Stop the session when top speed drops, not when the clock ends.

exercises.name: Bike Sprint Intervals
exercises.cue: Seat height so the knee is almost straight at the bottom. All-out 20 seconds, easy spin 100 seconds, repeat.

exercises.name: Stationary Bike Zone 2
exercises.cue: Steady resistance you can hold for the full block, cadence around 85. Lowest-stress way to add cardio on a tight-back week.

exercises.name: Elliptical Zone 2
exercises.cue: Upright posture, light hand contact, steady stride. Boring on purpose — this is recovery-friendly volume.

exercises.name: Rower Intervals
exercises.cue: Legs, then hips, then arms — never yank with the low back. Keep the spine tall; if the back rounds, end the set.

exercises.name: Lactate Threshold Run
exercises.cue: Comfortably hard pace you could hold for an hour, held for 8-20 minutes. Breathing should be rhythmic and controlled, not ragged.
